question: A network administrator attempts to automate the provisioning of several new Cisco Nexus switches. The administrator prepares a bootstrap configuration script for the task. Due to the number of switches, a zero-touch provisioning solution is preferred. Additionally, some switches arrive with outdated software and should be automatically upgraded as part of the provisioning workflow. Which solution meets the requirements?
theory: POAP is purpose-built to both install/upgrade the software image and apply the configuration during a switch's very first boot with zero manual steps, which is exactly the combination of zero-touch provisioning plus automatic image upgrade described. Ansible can push configuration afterward but can't stage an unreachable, unconfigured switch from scratch, plain NX-API needs an already-reachable device, and DHCP alone only hands out an address — it doesn't install images or configuration. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 17 — Evaluate Automation and Orchestration Technologies)
